questions.q: Which two clauses are required in every SOQL query?
options: FROM and ORDER BY
SELECT and WHERE
SELECT and FROM
SELECT and LIMIT
questions.explain: SELECT and FROM are the only required clauses; WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, LIMIT and others are all optional.

questions.q: What happens if you try to run SELECT * FROM Account in SOQL?
options: It fails — SOQL has no wildcard for selecting every field
It returns every field on the object, same as SQL
It returns only the Id field
It returns all fields but ignores custom fields
questions.explain: SOQL has no SELECT * equivalent. Every field you want back must be named explicitly in the field list.

questions.q: In Apex, what happens if you reference a field on a queried record that you did NOT include in the SELECT list?
options: Apex automatically re-queries the missing field
It silently returns null
It silently returns an empty string
A runtime error, not a silent null
questions.explain: Only fields named in the SELECT list are populated on returned sObjects; referencing an un-queried field throws a runtime error.

questions.q: What determines the order fields appear in a SOQL query's results?
options: The object's internal field definition order
The order the fields were listed in the SELECT clause
Alphabetical order
The order the fields were created in Setup
questions.explain: Fields return in exactly the order you listed them after SELECT, independent of the object's internal field order.

questions.q: Which statement about SOQL is true?
options: SOQL requires a semicolon in the Developer Console Query Editor
SOQL can insert new records with an INSERT INTO clause
SOQL is read-only; it never inserts, updates, or deletes records
SOQL can run against any relational database, not just Salesforce
questions.explain: SOQL only retrieves records. Creating, changing, or removing records happens through Apex DML statements (insert, update, delete, upsert), not SOQL.
